A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ANFM research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ANFM experiments on synthetic graphs, proteins, and GuacaMol, together with generation timings and extensive ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds training-cost comparisons and supplementary generation-quality results.

M1.justification: The filtration strategies, noise augmentation, graph mixer, Bernoulli-mixture decoder, teacher-forcing/PPO training, and post-hoc VAE labeling are retained. Expanded encoding and filtration descriptions document existing components rather than establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate small planar/SBM datasets, expanded planar/SBM/lobster datasets, protein graphs, and GuacaMol molecules. The additional analyses reuse this coverage without introducing new tasks or input scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the corresponding benchmark and ablation comparisons is retained. Newly discussed methods such as SID and DeFoG are citations, not additional evaluated baselines; the added step analysis retains the ANFM–DiGress comparison.

E3.justification: v2 extends evaluation with stage-specific and total H100 training hours in Table 29 and MMD metrics for the existing generation-step sweep in Figure 7. The benchmark splits, training budgets, hyperparameters, and 40/1024-sample evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix L adds four MMD curves examining generation quality versus step count, and Appendix K adds a training-versus-inference cost analysis. Existing component ablations are retained: the teacher-forcing experiment in v2 Table 6 already appeared in v1 Table 26.

E5.justification: v2 Table 27 adds analytical standard deviations for validity estimates using DiGress's approximately 56.2% SBM validity at sample sizes 32–1024. These are illustrative calculations, not additional repeated experiments. The three-run median/maximum-deviation practice is unchanged and receives further explanation in Appendix F.1.

E6.justification: New results include Figure 7's MMD curves and Table 29's ANFM/DiGress training costs: 60/95, 121/90, and 82/48 H100-hours for expanded planar, SBM, and lobster datasets, respectively. Table 27 adds analytical uncertainty values. Main benchmark scores are retained; the finer precision of DiGress's lobster degree MMD does not establish a performance change.

T1.justification: Appendix M explicitly adds the qualification that the line-Fiedler function is non-unique, including eigenvector sign ambiguity. Section 4.3 also corrects temporal mixing's lower time index from 1 to 0. The existing complexity propositions, evidence-bound derivation, and validity-estimator proof are retained.

C1.justification: The main generalization, graph-quality, and approximately 100-fold inference-speed claims remain. The revised conclusion qualifies the benefit of flexible filtrations by acknowledging that line-Fiedler sequences often underperform DFS, while emphasizing non-monotonic generation and its training strategies as the principal performance drivers.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses higher training costs on some datasets, implementation dependence of runtime comparisons, and the frequent advantage of DFS over line-Fiedler filtrations. It also distinguishes molecule-specific baselines from general graph generators and acknowledges the strong LSTM results. These qualify the retained performance narrative.

D1.justification: Appendix E.2 newly specifies the Laplacian, random-walk, and cycle-count features; Appendix M details the existing filtration construction. Appendix K reports training hardware/time breakdowns and filtration-preparation costs. Existing hyperparameter tables, training pseudocode, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of concurrent SID and citations concerning molecular generation, FCD, and spectral constructions, while removing v1's Pard comparison and several citations. Much of the RL and diffusion positioning is relocated from v1 Appendix A rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are rewritten, related work is reorganized by generation paradigm, and material from the extended related-work appendix is integrated into Sections 2 and 4.5. The teacher-forcing discussion moves into the main ablations, explanations expand across several sections, and the appendix contents page and impact statement are removed.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two-column main text with a single-column layout and extensively resizes and relocates displays. Table 1 places datasets side by side; Figure 1 incorporates filtration illustrations already shown in the appendix. The teacher-forcing table moves into the main text, while Figure 7 and Tables 27 and 29 are new displays.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through explicit training-cost tradeoffs, more detailed feature definitions, and clearer qualifications of the filtration and performance claims. The additional MMD curves strengthen the short-step evaluation. These are useful but limited gains because the method and main empirical evidence remain unchanged; removing the Pard discussion modestly reduces related-work coverage.
